title: Committee of Supply – Head R (Ministry of Law)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head R (Ministry of Law)

sections.label: Reviewing key legislation
sections.summary: Singapore will review key legislation this year, including reforms in arbitration, corporate insolvency and IP, to keep laws fit for purpose.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In order to achieve this, Singapore must constantly refresh its legal frameworks in an ever-changing and fast-evolving world, and also do it in a timely manner.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will therefore be reviewing key legislation with a view to updating them to ensure that our laws stay fit for purpose.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This will include, this year, reforms in arbitration, corporate insolvency and IP.

sections.label: Maxwell Chambers dispute resolution institutions
sections.summary: Maxwell Chambers hosts the highest concentration of international dispute resolution institutions, and three more institutions join Singapore this year, including ICSID.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Maxwell Chambers continues to serve as a leading dispute resolution complex, hosting the highest concentration of international dispute resolution institutions worldwide.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This year, we welcome three more institutions to Singapore: first, the International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID); second, the Shanghai International Arbitration Centre; and third, the Shenzhen Court of International Arbitration.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Besides being the first office outside its Washington DC headquarters, ICSID will join the four other World Bank Group organisations already based in Singapore, making Singapore the first country in the world to host local offices for all five World Bank organisations.

sections.label: ASEAN Treaty on Extradition
sections.summary: The AET requires at least six ASEAN member states to complete domestic procedures and notify the ASEAN Secretary-General that they are ready to bring it into effect.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To Ms Sylvia Lim’s query on the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Treaty on Extradition (AET), the AET requires at least six ASEAN members states to complete their respective domestic procedures and notify the ASEAN Secretary-General that they are ready to bring the AET into effect.

sections.label: Foreign firms and legal services exports
sections.summary: Foreign firms more than doubled and foreign lawyers more than quadrupled since 2000, and legal services exports rose eight-fold; a decision on the Committee's Report will be shared shortly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Foreign firms have more than doubled and foreign lawyers have more than quadrupled since the year 2000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Indeed, over the same period of time, since the year 2000, our legal services exports have gone up eight-fold, which shows that when we bring it together – foreign lawyers, Singapore practitioners at the core – we can extract value.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To Ms Lee’s query, we have studied the recommendations by the Committee to Review the Regulatory Framework for Law Practices and Collaborations and gathered feedback from a public consultation and our industry engagements, and we will share our decision on the Committee’s Report shortly.

sections.label: Civil legal aid means-test
sections.summary: Civil legal aid is available to households with a per capita household income of $1,050, and the means-test criteria will be raised to $1,650.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Today, civil legal aid is available to the bottom 25th percentile of households with a per capita household income (PCHI) of $1,050.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will raise the means-test criteria to a PCHI of $1,650.

sections.label: SLA state properties and land
sections.summary: The Singapore Land Authority manages around 2,600 state properties and 11,000 hectares of state land, equivalent to some 15,000 football fields.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Singapore Land Authority (SLA) manages a substantial portfolio of around 2,600 state properties and 11,000 hectares of state land – the equivalent of some 15,000 football fields.

sections.label: Mr Wong's term renewed
sections.summary: In January this year, Mr Wong's term was renewed for three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In January this year, Mr Wong's term was renewed for three years.

sections.label: Attorney-General appointment constitutional process
sections.summary: Article 35 requires the Prime Minister to consult the Chief Justice and PSC Chairman before advising the President, who then consults the CPA and assesses independently.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In the appointment of an AG, Article 35 of the Constitution provides that the Prime Minister must first consult the Chief Justice and the Chairman of the Public Service Commission (PSC) before tendering his advice as to the appointment to the President.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: After receiving that advice, the President in turn consults the Council of Presidential Advisers (CPA) and makes an independent assessment of the appointment.

sections.label: Public debate politicising non-partisan office
sections.summary: Turning it into a public debate risks politicising an office that must remain scrupulously non-partisan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Turning it into a public debate risks politicising an office that must remain scrupulously non-partisan.

sections.label: Mr Wong re-appointed after consultations
sections.summary: After considering all factors and required consultations, the Prime Minister advised the President to re-appoint Mr Wong for another term.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: He remains fit, able and willing to continue.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: So, having considered all these factors and after the required consultations, the Prime Minister advised the President to re-appoint Mr Wong for another term based on the constitutional mechanism.

sections.label: Legal AI use and legaltech funding
sections.summary: A Thomson Reuters survey found generative AI use roughly tripled since 2024, legaltech funding reached US$5.99 billion in 2025, and the Supreme Court uses AI transcription.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Based on Thomson Reuters' survey findings last month, the proportion of legal professionals using generative AI in their organisation has roughly tripled since 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Legaltech funding in 2025 reached US$5.99 billion, up from US$3.88 in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Supreme Court's own Court Audio Services System integrates audio recording and automated AI-driven transcription technology, allowing real-time conversion of spoken words into written text.

sections.label: Future of the Legal Profession Committee
sections.summary: The Future of the Legal Profession Committee will study some of these issues, working with the profession and broader legal industry to find a solution.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Some of these issues will be studied by the Future of the Legal Profession Committee, which I spoke about earlier, and we will have to work with the profession and the broader legal industry to understand these issues deeply and come together to find a solution.

sections.label: MinLaw legal industry gathering
sections.summary: MinLaw is organising a legal industry gathering on 6 March titled "The Next Charter: Shaping Singapore's Legal Future Together".

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As a first step, MinLaw is organising a gathering of the legal industry later this week, we titled it, "The Next Charter: Shaping Singapore's Legal Future Together" on 6 March.

sections.label: MinLaw as engaged partner
sections.summary: MinLaw will be an active, present and engaged partner, investing in people and institutions, and the legal system that navigates changes wisely will command greater trust.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: On this endeavour, what I can assure this House of is that MinLaw will not be a spectator.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will be an active, present and engaged partner – listening carefully and investing purposefully in our people and in our institutions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: And the legal system that navigates these changes wisely will command far greater trust and attract more commerce and investment, than one that responds with uncritical enthusiasm, or perhaps, unexamined fear.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The 1826 Charter of Justice gave Singapore a foundation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Now it falls to us – this generation, to ensure that the next chapter is worthy of all that came before it.

sections.label: MinLaw three development ways
sections.summary: MinLaw will steward development in three ways: empowering businesses through IP, facilitating dispute resolution, and growing the legal profession's capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: MinLaw will steward the next bound of our development in three ways: first, the private – empowering businesses through IP as an engine of growth; second, the public – facilitating resolution of disputes by deepening capabilities and reliability of our dispute resolution pathways; and third, the people – to grow the capabilities of our legal profession.

sections.label: ASME WIPO MOU IP centre
sections.summary: ASME and WIPO will exchange an MOU to set up the WIPO IP Business Centre @ ASME, the first in ASEAN.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: For example, the Association of Small and Medium Enterprises (ASME) and the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) will exchange a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) in a few days to set up the WIPO IP Business Centre @ ASME – the first in ASEAN.

sections.label: IPOS IA valuation guidelines
sections.summary: IPOS will support partners in publishing the IA valuation guidelines this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: IPOS will support our partners in publishing the IA valuation guidelines this year.

sections.label: MinLaw IPOS public consultation
sections.summary: MinLaw and IPOS will conduct a public consultation later this year on potential refinements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: To take our work further, MinLaw and IPOS will conduct a public consultation later this year on potential refinements.

sections.label: MinLaw legal industry thrusts
sections.summary: MinLaw works with industry on education and professionalisation, legaltech adoption, and opportunities in emerging areas such as ESG.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: MinLaw is working with industry on three thrusts: first, education and professionalisation – to deepen the strength of our legal industry; second, adoption of legaltech – to reduce repetitive, low-value tasks; and third, providing opportunities in emerging areas of work, such as the environmental, social and governance (ESG) sector.

sections.label: SAL competency framework publication
sections.summary: SAL published a national legal sector competency framework for disputes and corporate lawyers and in-house counsel, with a roadmap for allied professionals by 2027.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: In the professional sphere, SAL has published the national legal sector competency framework for disputes and corporate lawyers and in-house counsel.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: By 2027, a framework and training roadmap for allied legal professionals will follow.

sections.label: LIFT pilot and GenAI guide
sections.summary: Change management and cost challenge smaller firms; the LIFT pilot launched in June 2025 with seven SLPs, and a public consultation on a GenAI guide drew over 20 responses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: Change management remains a challenge, especially for smaller Singapore Law Practices (SLPs) alongside cost.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: We launched the pilot of the Legal Innovation and Future-Readiness Transformation (LIFT) initiative in June 2025 to support these firms to diagnose technology needs and implement tailored legaltech solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: To date, seven SLPs have joined the pilot.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: Second, we are ensuring responsible GenAI use – a point raised by Mr Nair.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: We conducted a public consultation in September 2025 on the draft Guide for Using GenAI in the Legal Sector and received over 20 constructive responses.

sections.label: Flock arts hub at Kampong Java
sections.summary: SLA collaborated with NAC to transform state properties at Kampong Java Road into Flock, an artist-led innovation and creation hub.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Responding to arts practitioners' call for a dedicated space, SLA collaborated with the National Arts Council (NAC) to transform state properties at Kampong Java Road, into "Flock" – an artist-led innovation and creation hub.

sections.label: Adam Park bungalow cluster sale
sections.summary: SLA recently launched the sale of the Adam Park heritage bungalow cluster on a 30-year lease.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: For instance, SLA recently launched the sale of the Adam Park heritage bungalow cluster on a 30-year lease.

sections.label: Settlement rate and mandatory mediation
sections.summary: About 80% of cases reach an amicable settlement, which is why it was made mandatory.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: About 80% of cases reach an amicable settlement and that is why we made it mandatory.

sections.label: Simplifying civil judgment enforcement
sections.summary: MinLaw aims to simplify enforcement by giving courts asset-identification powers, new enforcement modes and Civil Judgment Enforcement Officers, with a Bill planned this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We aim to simplify the enforcement process, therefore, to be more effective, efficient and affordable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We intend to do this by: one, giving the Court greater powers to identify a judgment debtor's assets and means; two, by introducing new enforcement modes to deter and punish non-compliance with Court orders; and three, creating new Civil Judgment Enforcement Officers to assist parties with enforcing their civil judgments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We have been consulting with relevant stakeholders, including the Bar and the Judiciary, and aim to introduce a Bill later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Since establishing the new Maintenance Enforcement Division in January last year, the Family Justice Courts have referred around 1,000 cases to the new Division.

sections.label: Expanding civil legal aid coverage
sections.summary: Civil legal aid PCHI threshold rises from $1,050 to $1,650, and bank savings and non-CPF investment thresholds rise from $10,000 to $12,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: As the Minister announced earlier, we will expand civil legal aid coverage by the LAB.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We will raise the PCHI threshold for civil legal aid from $1,050 to $1,650.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: This could potentially benefit up to 1,000 more Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents annually.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: To account for rising household income, the bank savings and non-Central Provident Fund investment threshold for both civil legal aid and criminal defence aid will be raised from $10,000 to $12,000 to ensure that the truly needy remain eligible.

sections.label: Inclusive Justice Taskforce launch
sections.summary: MinLaw launched the Inclusive Justice Taskforce in January to examine support for individuals with conditions and disabilities who risk offending or interact with the criminal justice system.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: These questions intersect multiple areas such as law, social services and healthcare, and involve stakeholders from the private and public sector.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Thus, MinLaw formally announced the launch of the Inclusive Justice Taskforce (IJT) in January this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The IJT will examine how society can better support individuals with such conditions and disabilities who risk offending or who interact with the criminal justice system.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: It is to raise public awareness of what works and recommend tangible improvements.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The IJT has begun its work and we will provide updates in due course.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: I am also grateful for the IJT members across the private and public sectors – lawyers, policy-makers, law enforcement officers, social service professionals, healthcare experts, community partners and caregiver representatives.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We will enhance legal services and intellectual property to support the economy, uphold the rule of law and expand access to justice and, at the same time, optimise land to meet our community needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: As we commemorate the bicentennial anniversary of the Second Charter of Justice this year, we look not only to our own history but to the future – one where the law continues to serve Singapore and Singaporeans well.

sections.label: State Courts Services Hub assistance
sections.summary: About 400 CDRT-related enquiries were handled by the State Courts Services Hub last year, which assists applicants case by case through the service journey.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: On the next question about the cases, about 400 CDRT-related enquiries last year were handled by the State Courts Services Hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: So, that means if an applicant needs to file the claim but does not know how to do it, can the hub actually help them to do it step by step rather than say, "You just do this, do this" and then you go back home and do it on your own.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: I think the Service Hub provides assistance on a case by case basis, and to the best of their ability in each case to really walk through the service journey with each individual user.

sections.label: AMDs in future care plans
sections.summary: The Minister says AMDs are one instrument that can potentially be looked at for a full suite of future care plans instruments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: On the second part about AMDs, I understand that to look at it comprehensively for a full suite of future care plans instruments, AMD definitely is one of the instruments that we can potentially look at.

sections.label: Exploring increased Wills Registry search fees
sections.summary: The Minister says exploring increased search fees instead of waiving fees is something to take back and consider.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: The first question is, can we explore rather than to not totally include or consider the waiver of fees, instead can we explore increasing the search fees instead, so as to achieve the objectives that Senior Parliamentary Secretary had mentioned in terms of defraying the fees for maintaining such a services in the Wills Registry?

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: I think that is something we can explore and we will take it back to consider.

sections.label: PDO resourcing and caseload
sections.summary: Asks whether PDO is adequately resourced to ensure access and manageable caseloads for lawyers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My second clarification question has to do with the resourcing of PDO to ensure that there is access and a manageable case load for the lawyers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I think it is good that legal access is made more available to more Singaporeans, but I think we also want to ensure that the quality of service is comparable, and so whether PDO is adequately resourced; how does the Ministry think about that?

sections.label: PDO cases and staffing
sections.summary: PDO cases exceeded 2,300 last year, with 22 full-time public defender officers and shared caseload with CLAS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Since we started the PDO, the number of cases, applications have gone up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Last year, it was in excess of 2,300.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: When we set up PDO, we had a plan to scale up our resources and manpower, expecting that the numbers would rise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We are also working with Criminal Legal Aid Scheme (CLAS) to share the case load; and so that is manageable for the foreseeable future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We now have grown the PDO with 22 public defender officers, and they are full-time, they are very professional and dedicated.

sections.label: AG appointment shortlist question
sections.summary: Asks the Prime Minister to confirm he did not shortlist other candidates in the recent AG appointment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One, can he confirm then that the Prime Minister did not shortlist any other candidates in the recent round of appointment of AG?

sections.label: Community disputes mandatory mediation
sections.summary: The Community Disputes Resolution Act sets a low threshold for mediation directions, making mediation mandatory in community disputes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Broadly, although I know that they currently apply to consensual mediation, 80% of cases are resolved amicably through mediation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: More importantly, in the context of community disputes where you are talking about two neighbours who live in proximity to one another, we think that it is, in fact, the most appropriate means by which you should resolve a dispute.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, we have designed the enhanced framework in the Community Disputes Resolution Act, which we passed in Parliament some months ago as having a lower threshold for driving parties to mediation, and in this case, mandatory mediation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We think that in most cases, matters ought to be resolved in the first instance and maybe even in the second instance through mediation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Therefore, the threshold for issuing a mediation direction is low.

sections.label: Tampines pilot expansion study
sections.summary: The Tampines pilot is being studied for expansion, including other functions of the CRU.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In terms of an expansion, let me say that we are studying the pilot that is being conducted at Tampines, learning from the experiences, understanding the processes and streamlining it, and in some cases, finetuning it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We are thinking about what more can be done and we are studying the expansion, both in terms of the pilot, as well as thinking about what other functions of the CRU can be expanded.

sections.label: 2022 family proceedings reforms
sections.summary: In 2022, reforms were studied to make family proceedings simpler, more efficient, more affordable and less acrimonious.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For example, in 2022, reforms were studied to improve family proceedings so that they would be simpler, more efficient, more affordable and less acrimonious.

sections.label: MinLaw disability justice taskforce
sections.summary: In 2026 MinLaw launched a taskforce to better support persons with disabilities and mental health conditions in the criminal justice system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Most recently, in 2026, MinLaw launched a new taskforce to better support persons with disabilities and mental health conditions in the criminal justice system.

sections.label: AI cited fictitious cases
sections.summary: In one reported case, the Court found a litigant in person relying on AI tools cited six fictitious cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In one reported case, the Court found that a litigant in person who relied on AI tools to generate legal submissions cited six fictitious cases.

sections.label: Workplace principles for legal practice
sections.summary: Last year the Ethics and Professional Standards Committee recommended the Singapore Academy of Law develop core workplace principles for legal practice sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Last year, the Ethics and Professional Standards Committee recommended that the Singapore Academy of Law develop a core set of workplace principles aimed at maintaining the sustainability of legal practice.

sections.label: Consultation on GenAI guide
sections.summary: Last year MinLaw conducted a public consultation on a proposed Guide for Using GenAI in the Legal Sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Last year, MinLaw conducted a public consultation on a proposed Guide for Using GenAI in the Legal Sector.

sections.label: Responsible AI use and ASEAN extradition
sections.summary: The passage states lawyers should use AI responsibly, and that in November last year ASEAN member states signed the ASEAN Treaty on Extradition in Manila.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As the Court observed in one case, such actions by lawyers cast a shadow over the legitimacy and honour of the legal profession and its role as a custodian of justice in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Therefore, the question is not whether lawyers should use AI, but how AI can be used responsibly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: With clear guidance and training, legal professionals can improve productivity with AI while safeguarding the accuracy of work products and their confidentiality and ethical obligations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This is important as we continue to position Singapore as a leading international hub for legal services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Chairman, ultimately, access to justice and the growth of Singapore as a legal hub are mutually reinforcing goals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Chairman, in November last year in Manila, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) member states signed up to the ASEAN Treaty on Extradition.

sections.label: Extradition treaty ratification questions
sections.summary: The passage asks what needs to be done before ratification of the treaty and whether Singapore has indicated its ratification.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, I understand that the treaty is not yet enforced, as it requires six member states to ratify it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: What needs to be done before ratification, and has Singapore indicated its ratification?

sections.label: Waiving Wills Registry fees
sections.summary: The speaker proposes waiving the $50 registration fee and $50 update fee for wills deposited with the SAL Wills Registry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: My first proposal is to waive the $50 registration fee and the $50 update fee for every will deposited with the Singapore Academy of Law's (SAL's) Wills Registry.

sections.label: Neighbour dispute claims filed
sections.summary: Between 2020 and 2024, only 1,031 claims were filed, a fraction of the 2,500 neighbour dispute cases reported to HDB monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Between 2020 and 2024, only 1,031 claims were filed, a fraction of the 2,500 neighbour dispute cases reported to HDB monthly.

sections.label: Attorney-General reappointed fourth term
sections.summary: In October last year, the AGC announced the President had reappointed the Attorney-General for a fourth three-year term until January 2029.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Chairman, in October last year, the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) announced that the President had reappointed the Attorney-General (AG) for a fourth term of three years until January 2029.

sections.label: Shortlisting candidates before AG reappointment
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Prime Minister shortlisted other candidates before recommending the Attorney-General's reappointment for a fourth three-year term.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Did the Prime Minister shortlist other candidates before recommending the reappointment of the AG for a fourth three-year term?

sections.label: Darren Tang WIPO reappointment
sections.summary: Darren Tang's appointment as WIPO Director-General and reappointment for a second term reflect the strength of Singapore's legal and IP ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For example, the appointment of Mr Darren Tang as Director-General of WIPO as well as his successful reappointment for a second term reflects the strength of Singapore's legal and IP ecosystem, and that our ability to produce thought leadership organically from within our own system and our own country.

sections.label: Rena Lee ICJ candidacy
sections.summary: Singapore has put up Ambassador Rena Lee as its candidate to the International Court of Justice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For example, we have put up Ambassador Rena Lee as our candidate to the International Court of Justice.

sections.label: Mediation convention ratification update
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister for an update on countries ratifying the convention, mediator dispute take-up, and MinLaw's efforts to rally international support for Singapore as a global mediation hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Could the Minister provide an update on the number of countries that have ratified the convention, the take-up of mediator disputes under it and how MinLaw will continue to rally international support to strengthen Singapore's role as a global mediation hub?

sections.label: New lawyers likely to leave
sections.summary: The Chief Justice shared surveys showing around 60% of newly minted lawyers said they were likely to leave legal practice in the next five years, citing workload, work-life balance, mental well-being, flexible work arrangements and workplace culture.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: At the Opening of the Legal Year last month, our Chief Justice shared that surveys of newly minted lawyers in the last two years showed that around 60% of respondents said they were likely to leave legal practice in the next five years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They cited reasons, such as excessive workload, poor work-life balance affecting their mental well-being, a lack of flexible work arrangements and poor workplace culture.

sections.label: Initiatives for legal profession challenges
sections.summary: The Chief Justice announced initiatives to address these challenges and will co-lead with the Law Minister in setting the direction of the Future of the Legal Profession Committee.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our Chief Justice has announced a slew of initiatives to address these challenges and he will be co-leading with our Law Minister in setting the direction of the Future of the Legal Profession Committee to help the legal profession meet these challenges ahead.

sections.label: Small law firms need more help
sections.summary: The passage states most law firms are small businesses with fewer resources, and hopes future-proofing and retaining talent will look beyond technological solutions to morale, career insecurity in the age of AI, and financial and business stress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Let us not forget that most of our law firms are small businesses, who have far fewer resources and may need a lot more help.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is my hope that in looking to future-proofing the legal profession and to retain and nurture talent, we will look at more than technological solutions, and understand that the issues relating to morale, career insecurity in the age of AI, financial and business stress are just as important.

sections.label: Report on law practice regulatory framework
sections.summary: The Committee Report on the regulatory framework for law practices proposed changes to Qualifying Foreign Law Practices and caps on Singapore lawyers in FLPs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: The Committee Report on the regulatory framework for law practices proposed changes to Qualifying Foreign Law Practices (QFLPs) and caps on Singapore lawyers in FLPs.

sections.label: MinLaw support for in-house counsel
sections.summary: MinLaw said at the Asia-Pacific Legal Congress 2024 that it is committed to better support in-house legal counsel.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: MinLaw said at the Asia-Pacific Legal Congress 2024, that MinLaw is committed to better support in-house legal counsel.

sections.label: ESG Legal Secondment Programme
sections.summary: A March 2025 PwC report led MinLaw to introduce the ESG Legal Secondment Programme for Singapore-qualified lawyers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In March 2025, a report was jointly commissioned by MinLaw, the Economic Development Board and Enterprise Singapore, and independently researched by PriceWaterhouseCoopers (PwC), titled "Sustainability Ready Singapore Lawyers".

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In response, the Ministry introduced the ESG Legal Secondment Programme, allowing Singapore-qualified lawyers to be seconded into corporate sustainability teams to gain hands-on experience.

sections.label: Programme uptake and feedback
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister for a snapshot of the programme, including uptake and feedback so far.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gho Sze Kee (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Would the Minister provide a snapshot of this programme, including the level of uptake and feedback thus far?

sections.label: Legal and land-use architecture
sections.summary: The passage states there may be scope to consider how legal and land-use architecture can support Singapore as a regional sports and entertainment hub.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As we build on this trajectory, there may be scope to consider how our legal and land-use architecture can further support Singapore's evolution into a regional sports and entertainment hub.

sections.label: Sports and entertainment arbitration
sections.summary: The question asks whether specialised capabilities in sports and entertainment arbitration and mediation could be developed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could we further develop specialised capabilities in sports and entertainment arbitration and mediation, positioning Singapore as a regional hub for related commercial disputes?

sections.label: Tenure certainty for organisations
sections.summary: The question asks whether greater tenure certainty could be explored for organisations demonstrating clear community impact.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Kenneth Goh (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Working with agencies such as the Singapore Land Authority (SLA), could we explore greater tenure certainty for organisations that demonstrate clear community impact?

sections.label: Expanding attachment schemes for SMEs
sections.summary: The question asks whether there are plans to expand and scale attachment schemes for growth-oriented SMEs commercialising IP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Government elaborate on whether there are plans to expand and scale such attachment schemes, particularly for growth-oriented SMEs seeking to commercialise IP?

sections.label: State-backed IP financing risk-sharing
sections.summary: Asks whether the Government would consider calibrated state-backed risk-sharing mechanisms to catalyse IP financing so financial institutions lend against viable IP assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Would the Government consider calibrated state-backed risk-sharing mechanisms to catalyse IP financing so that financial institutions are more willing to lend against viable IP assets while risks remain prudently managed?

sections.label: Means test revision 2024
sections.summary: The means test was last revised in 2024, raising per capita household income to $1,050 and the Annual Value threshold to $21,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The means test was last revised in 2024, with the per capita household income raised to $1,050 and the Annual Value threshold to $21,000.

sections.label: Sufficiency of income threshold
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry considers the current $1,050 per capita income threshold sufficient given rising costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, does the Ministry consider the current $1,050 per capita income threshold sufficient, given rising costs?

sections.label: MinLaw and IPOS IP capabilities
sections.summary: Asks how MinLaw and IPOS are helping businesses, especially SMEs, build IP capabilities and strengthen Singapore as a global IP hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: They need strong enforcement, proper valuation, financing support and trusted dispute resolution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, I ask: how are MinLaw and IPOS helping businesses, especially our SMEs, build stronger IP capabilities so that IP becomes a real business asset, not just legal protection?

sentences.speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As we move into the next phase of IP Strategy 2030, what more can be done to strengthen Singapore as a global hub for IP dispute resolution, valuation and licensing, especially in new sectors?

sections.label: Civil enforcement process enhancements
sections.summary: Notes a successful litigant must invest time and resources with no guarantee of recovery, and the Minister said the Ministry was studying enhancements to civil enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: It requires a successful litigant to invest more time and resources with no guarantee of recovery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: It was therefore heartening when the Minister announced during COS 2024 and 2025 that the Ministry was studying potential enhancements to the civil enforcement process, such as giving the Courts greater powers to identify the assets and means of judgment debtors in order to help the judgment creditor make an informed decision on whether and how to enforce the judgment.

sections.label: Maintenance Enforcement Process officers
sections.summary: Operationalised in January 2025 with progressive expansion, Maintenance Enforcement Process officers can obtain financial information, facilitate conciliation and provide reports to assist judges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Operationalised in January 2025, with progressive expansion in phases, we now have Maintenance Enforcement Process officers who can obtain financial information, facilitate conciliation and provide reports to assist judges.

sections.label: Legal aid income eligibility percentiles
sections.summary: Criminal defence aid is pegged at around the 35th percentile of resident households by per capita household income, while civil legal aid remains roughly at the 25th percentile.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Currently, criminal defence aid under the Public Defender's Office is pegged at around the 35th percentile of resident households by per capita household income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Civil legal aid, however, remains roughly at the 25th percentile.

sections.label: Civil enforcement reform study
sections.summary: The Ministry said in previous debates it was studying reforms to strengthen civil enforcement, including powers to identify judgment debtors' assets and deterrence against non-compliance with Court orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, in previous debates, the Ministry said it was studying reforms to strengthen civil enforcement, including greater powers to identify the assets of judgment debtors and stronger deterrence against non-compliance with Court orders.

sections.label: Review status and amendment timeline
sections.summary: The speaker asks what the current status of the Ministry's review is and when legislative amendments or pilot measures will be introduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It must ensure that its decisions are obeyed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I therefore ask, what is the current status of the Ministry’s review?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: When will we see legislative amendments or pilot measures introduced?

sections.label: Review of legal aid eligibility criteria
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry will review legal aid eligibility criteria to ensure continued accessibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: First, will the Ministry review legal aid eligibility criteria to ensure continued accessibility?
